rv.q: Cappiello’s precision-guided satire stitches together three thematically similar but distinct standalone short plays.
Beyond their dubious humor, these overextended one-acts intend to comment seriously upon women being forced to submit to misguided patriarchal authority.
What writer-director Katie Cappiello has wrought are three stories on serious matters.
Katie Cappiello’s The Body of Mary: A Play in Three Acts (of God) is as funny as it is frightening.

cn.t: Critics are largely impressed by Cappiello's provocative triptych examining the Catholic Church's treatment of women, praising its biting humor and emotional punch, though one reviewer finds the comedic approach to serious topics misguided.
